answer: This checkpoint's compiler-tree search genuinely needs well beyond 30s per record, independent of lexer cost. The lexer-cache fix is real and is being exercised on this exact decode path (build_scanner calls near-zero) -- it cut per-call compiler_ms by 2.0x-11.1x. But removing the lexer-rebuild tax exposed the next cost layer (Lark's accepts() probe + un-shared per-candidate witness-search memoization), so total wall-clock stayed pinned at ~30s: fewer ms per call, but 2x-11x more calls now complete (13-76 tokens emitted, zero dead-ends post-fix vs 7-8 tokens and 1/1 dead-end pre-fix), because genuine previously-masked decode progress now happens instead of an early swallowed-timeout dead-end.
